graph.name: christmas-bell-smd
graph.description: Automatic Christmas bell, variant SMD (D-11): the circuit of the main board with 0805 LEDs, an SMD servo header and an SMD buffer capacitor; JLCPCB's Economic assembly places everything but the Nano's female headers.

purpose.notes: Automatic Christmas bell, SMD variant, for the owner's home, built and used by the owner – not sold or given away (D-16). Powered from a USB port or power bank through the Nano's USB; no battery holder, no mains, no radio.

conventions.pin_reference: '<designator>.<pin>' with the pin numbers of the EasyEDA symbol
conventions.v: per net: [min, max] in V over all operating states
conventions.waive: per net or component: {check id: reason} accepts a finding on purpose

hints.H-1: C1 1000 µF / 16 V electrolytic on +5V, next to J1 (it buffers the Nano's 5V pin)
hints.H-7: J1 is the servo's own cable inside the bell's frame, plugged once; no TVS – like the main board

components.label: Arduino Nano 3 (plugged in)

waive.P-1: VIN stays free: the Nano runs from its USB socket

components.notes: Plugs into two 1x15 female headers, pitch 2.54 mm (hand-soldered, not in the graph). Powered through its USB socket; its 5V pin (USB minus a Schottky diode) supplies the servo, C1 and the buttons. Pin names are the library symbol's ATmega port names; its labels of pins 14/15 are swapped (pin 14 = D11 = PB3, pin 15 = D12 = PB4 on the Nano).

components.label: Servo (GND, +5 V, signal), SMD header
components.notes: Standard servo plug: brown = GND (1), red = +5 V (2), orange = signal (3). SMD header, placed by JLCPCB (D-11).

components.label: Buffer capacitor for the servo (SMD)
components.notes: Absorbs the servo's start-up peaks so the Nano does not reset. SMD can: the Economic assembly places it (D-11).

nets.notes: Pressed = 5 V at D11, else R7 pulls to GND (D-4).
